Use case: precise-object-edit. Production game sprite extraction and refinement for Worldgoing.
Reference image 1 is the approved military compound. Recreate ONLY ONE of its six repeated rectangular soldiers' dormitory buildings, without the compound, as a complete standalone sprite on genuinely transparent background. Choose the lower-left dormitory design.
South-facing view: a fixed elevated orthographic camera looking from the south, exactly like the reference. Long roof ridge runs horizontally across the image. Building is an unrotated rectangle, NOT diamond isometric. One front central door and four small windows, low stone footing, plain white plaster and dark timber beams, reddish brown tiled gable roof. No chimney, flag, emblem, sign, props, barrels, racks, fence, people, shadows on a ground plane, text or watermark.
Physical footprint 6 metres east-west by 4 metres north-south (3 by 2 game cells). Front wall about 2.6 metres high, door opening 2 metres high, practical low military dormitory, consistent full-sized human door. Roof depth reflects the 4m physical depth; do not make a tall cottage or tiny door. Neutral light from upper-left, hand-painted crisp detailed 2D strategy sprite with restrained dark contours matching the reference.
Center a single building with complete roof and foundation and comfortable transparent margin. Door threshold and stone foundation must be unobscured for ground calibration. No detached accessories. Output only the one sprite.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Reference image is the approved south-facing standalone military dormitory. Produce the SAME building viewed after a physical rotation around its vertical axis, for a four-direction Worldgoing sprite set. Keep the fixed elevated orthographic strategy-game camera from the south. Keep identical warm red tile material, white plaster, dark wood, low stone foundation, 6m-long by 4m-deep original footprint, 2.6m wall height, 2m door opening, crisp hand painted style and upper-left lighting. This is not a flat rotation of the image. The building must remain upright. Only one complete building on real transparent background, with margin. No glow, environment, ground, flags, emblems, props, people, chimney, words or extra objects. Rotate the building so its original long door-bearing facade now faces WEST, on the LEFT side of the image. The world footprint is now 4 metres east-west and 6 metres north-south. Its roof ridge runs vertically north-south in the image. The left long wall has the central door and four windows from the reference, viewed obliquely; the narrow gable end facing the camera/south has timber bracing and plaster, no door. Keep the west door/threshold visible enough to ground-anchor at the midpoint of the left wall. Strong orthographic overhead feel, not a diagonally turned diamond. Roof tiles run correctly down both roof slopes.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Fix ONLY the architectural scale of this south-facing dormitory sprite for a game with 2-metre grid cells. The current image's door is much too short for a full-sized human: its opening is only about 170 pixels high against a 1200-pixel foundation width.
CORRECTION IS MANDATORY: the door opening's clear VERTICAL height must be approximately ONE THIRD of the entire building's foundation width. For a 1200-pixel-wide foundation, make the door opening about 400 pixels tall. Front eaves/wall height about 520 pixels above the doorstep. Raise the roof to accommodate this taller wall; retain the same roof design, pitch and depth, same 6m building width by 4m ground depth. Use a taller transparent canvas if needed; do NOT squeeze the result into the old canvas. Door realistic human proportion (opening width about 160 pixels for height400), four windows resized/repositioned to the taller wall. Keep the full front facade white plaster/darktimber, low stone footing, red tile roof, exact same unrotated south-view camera and all existing materials.
One sprite only, NO person or height markers. Transparent background, no glow, ground, flag, text or props. Keep complete roof and foundation fully within the frame. This edit is about doubling the wall/door vertical height while keeping horizontal foundation width fixed.

Precise architectural scale correction of this same south-facing military dormitory, preserve all materials and camera. The door is still too short. Increase the DOOR OPENING VERTICAL HEIGHT by 50%, while preserving its width. Increase the whole white plaster front wall height by 50% too and move the roof upwards. Keep foundation width EXACTLY unchanged. Make a TALLER OUTPUT CANVAS to fit, preferably square. Do not scale the whole building down.
Target: foundation width about 1400 pixels, door clear opening height about 500 pixels measured straight down at its center. The door top-to-bottom height must clearly exceed one third of the foundation width. Eaves at least 550 pixels above doorstep. This is a 6-metre wide dormitory with a normal 2.1-metre HUMAN-SIZED door, not a toy model.
Keep one central door, four windows, modest red tiled roof, white plaster and dark timber, gray stone foundation. Preserve upper-left lighting. One building only; no characters, flags, text, props, ground, glow or border. Genuine transparent background. Complete roof fully inside canvas.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Reference is our FINAL correctly scaled south-facing military dormitory. Generate one other physical orientation of EXACTLY THE SAME BUILDING, keeping the same tall full-human door, wall height, roof material, white plaster/timber, stone foundation, sunlight and 2D handpainted game sprite style. Original footprint 6m wide along the long facade and 4m deep. Door is 2.2m high, eaves 3m. Keep this correct life-size scale; no tiny doors or squat front walls. The camera always stays at the same fixed elevated position south of the building. Complete single sprite on genuine transparent background, no ground, glow, shadow halo, chimney, flag, text, props, people, or extra objects. Physically rotate the building 90 degrees so its long door-bearing facade faces west (LEFT). World footprint is now 4 metres east-west, 6 metres north-south. Roof ridge runs north-south, nearly vertical in image; camera sees the narrow south gable end plus a slight view of the left long side. Door is midway along the LEFT side, with two windows on each side of it. The south gable wall is blank plaster with timber framing, no door. Door clear VERTICAL opening height should be approximately HALF the total foundation's left-to-right image width, since the world foundation width is now 4m and door height is2.2m. Raise wall height as necessary to retain this scale. This is critical: tall human-sized side door, not a tiny hatch. Do not turn the whole footprint into a diagonal diamond. Use portrait or square framing as needed.

Precise-object edit of ONLY the vertical architectural scale. Preserve this WEST-facing dormitory's exact roof, width, camera and orientation. The left long wall's door is too small: increase its clear VERTICAL opening height by approximately 65 percent, without changing its width. Raise BOTH visible plaster walls and roof to accommodate the taller door. Do not increase the horizontal foundation width.
Numerical visual target: whole stone foundation spans about 1030px horizontally. Door opening measured at its vertical center must be about 500px tall, not the current330px. Use a taller canvas if necessary. This represents a 4-metre-wide rotated footprint with a full-sized 2-metre human door. Keep one door on WEST/left long wall, four windows along that wall, and a plain blank SOUTH gable end. Door steps must remain visible. Keep exact red-tile style, pale plaster, wood beams, stone foundation, light from upper-left. One complete upright sprite on genuine transparent background, no ground, halo, characters, labels or props.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Adjust ONLY the camera yaw/projection of this same WEST-facing dormitory to fit an orthogonal grid-based game. The visible WEST/left long wall is currently too wide in screen X. Move the camera much closer to a straight SOUTH elevation, keeping its elevated pitch. The narrow south gable end should occupy about 85 percent of the building's total horizontal screen width; the left long wall should occupy only the remaining15percent, strongly foreshortened. The roof ridge is nearly vertical in the image, not diagonal. Keep the west door midway along the narrow visible LEFT long wall. Keep its existing absolute vertical height and threshold; compress only that side's horizontal projection as camera yaw changes. Keep the entire south gable wall rectangular with horizontal base edge, preserve its full height and width.
This is the same 4m east-west by6m north-south footprint. Keep tall human door, white plaster/dark timber, red tiled roof, stone base, upper-left lighting. One complete upright sprite, transparent alpha background, no floor or ground shadows, no props, people, text, flags, glow or halo. Do not crop roof or foundation.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Generate the EAST-facing counterpart of the exact dormitory shown. Mirror the building's GEOMETRY horizontally so the narrow visible long wall and its single full-height door move from LEFT to RIGHT. Preserve exactly the same shape, height, foundation width, strong foreshortening of the side wall, and nearly straight orthogonal SOUTH camera with elevated pitch. The south gable fills85percent of screen width and the right east wall only15percent. The roof ridge is nearly vertical. Preserve tall human-sized door opening: at least HALF of the total stone foundation horizontal width, which represents4m. The door is2.1m tall. Front south gable is blank plaster with structural timbers and no door.
Important lighting: although the geometry swaps sides, keep illumination coming from upper-left, repaint highlights accordingly; do not simply flip light direction. Keep all materials, warm red tiles, pale plaster, timber, stone foundation, complete roof, crisp 2D sprite style. One complete upright building centered on genuine TRANSPARENT alpha, no floor, glow, scenery, people, flag, text or props.

notes: Initial source candidates with undersized doors or broad side projection were superseded. No programmatic image editing; selected images copied byte-for-byte. Faction flags drawn separately by the original SiteResourceView.
